actions.label: Document the reuse of your work (1 workday)
actions.explain: You initiated the earlier water project because no one was meeting an unmet need. A later funding gap left unsafe access hours and harmed Mara. You take responsibility for starting the work and its effects, while control of maintenance and claims of sole blame remain disputed. The committee now uses your new plans while excluding you; spend a day recording what can be verified, without assuming a remedy.

actions.label: Ask police to review the documented conflict (1 workday)
actions.explain: The assigned officer discloses a working relationship with the committee chair, then closes the complaint without action. The record remains, but there is no remedy or restored credit.

actions.label: Bring the documented reuse into public view (1 workday)
actions.explain: Publicly describe what the records show and what remains disputed. More residents hear the case, but committee leaders frame it as disruptive; one supporter withdraws. Visibility is not proof or a legal remedy.

actions.label: Hear Mara's concerns (1 workday)
actions.explain: Mara wants a workshop budget and public access hours before she will support a solar proposal.

actions.label: Hear Eli's concerns (1 workday)
actions.explain: Eli wants maintenance responsibility and a clear account of grant spending before he will support the project.

actions.label: Convene a project committee (1 workday)
actions.explain: A committee needs a resident mandate. Convening it takes time before it can hold funds or make decisions.

actions.label: Seek a second resident's backing (1 workday)
actions.explain: One resident supports the project so far. Make time to hear another view; a broader mandate improves the chance of a grant.

actions.label: Write the scope and budget (2 coins + 1 workday)
actions.explain: You pay the travel and materials cost yourself to document access, maintenance, and a workable budget. This is unpaid preparation; no grant is promised.

actions.label: Submit the community grant application (1 coin + 1 workday)
actions.explain: The application fee and preparation are paid by you. Funding is uncertain: the decision arrives after the next rest, and one endorsement may not beat competing proposals.

actions.label: Revise and resubmit with both residents' backing (1 workday)
actions.explain: The first application was declined. You have another supporter now; spend a workday revising the case and try again.

actions.label: Fairly hire a local installer for the wiring (3 committee coins)
actions.explain: The committee pays a local installer to wire up the hardware, records your unpaid preparation, and keeps the maintenance and open-access terms. You still need to source and contribute the panel and inverter.

actions.label: Award the wiring contract to the chair’s associate (3 committee coins)
actions.explain: The committee pays the chair’s associate to wire up the hardware, but bypasses the unpaid contributor, gives them no credit, and drops the agreed maintenance term. The community can still benefit if the equipment is supplied; trust and future cooperation take a hit.

actions.label: Mismanage the grant (all 5 committee coins)
actions.explain: The committee loses the grant to untracked spending. There is no installer payment or finished work; the community remains without the service while an audit is requested.

actions.label: Organise community contributions (1 workday)
actions.explain: After the grant fails or is lost, bring residents together to raise a small, explicit pool. This takes time and community backing; the money belongs to the committee, not you.

actions.label: Carry the project yourself (3 coins + 1 workday)
actions.explain: If the grant fails, the committee loses the money, or community fundraising is not right for you, personally cover the remaining start-up costs. This does not repay the coins and work already spent.

actions.label: Buy a solar panel at the market (4 coins)
actions.explain: The market route: fast, but spends coins.

actions.label: Buy an inverter at the market (7 coins)
actions.explain: The market route: fast, but spends coins.

actions.label: Salvage a panel from the scrapyard (1 labour)
actions.explain: The labour route: keeps coins, spends a turn's work.

actions.label: Salvage an inverter from the scrapyard (1 labour)
actions.explain: The labour route: keeps coins, spends a turn's work.

actions.label: Install the panel into the solar project
actions.explain: Shared work: your part becomes community infrastructure.

actions.label: Install the inverter into the solar project
actions.explain: Shared work: your part becomes community infrastructure.

actions.label: Present the project at the committee meeting
actions.explain: The committee endorses a project once real parts are installed.

actions.label: Switch on the workshop solar system
actions.explain: Needs both parts installed AND committee endorsement.

actions.label: Improve the shelter with bought materials (3 coins)
actions.explain: Personal asset improvement via the market route.

actions.label: Patch the shelter yourself (1 labour)
actions.explain: Personal asset improvement via the labour route.

actions.label: Rest for the evening (regain labour)
actions.explain: Only useful once you've spent your labour.

actions.label: Repair the water tank with parts (3 coins)
actions.explain: Buy a replacement fitting and return the shared tank to service.

actions.label: Repair the water tank with salvaged fittings (1 labour)
actions.explain: Use time and repair skill instead of buying a new fitting.

actions.label: Plant the garden using shared water (1 labour)
actions.explain: The garden needs a working tank and one block of labour.

actions.label: Rebuild the canal bridge (1 labour)
actions.explain: The bridge crew needs working water and one block of labour. Finish by the end of day four before the canal rises.

actions.label: Brace the flooded bridge supports (1 labour)
actions.explain: After day four, the high canal needs a bracing shift before the usual crew can finish the bridge.

actions.label: Finish the braced bridge (1 labour)
actions.explain: The supports are braced. One more workday reopens the crossing without spending coins.

actions.label: Hire a canal crew to rebuild now (2 coins, 1 labour)
actions.explain: After day four, a specialist crew can work through the high water in one day. It costs two coins and your labour to coordinate.

actions.label: Commission the wind pump (1 labour)
actions.explain: The crossing must be restored and the workshop powered before the pump can be commissioned.

actions.label: Plant the Saltwind orchard (1 labour)
actions.explain: The orchard needs the commissioned wind pump and one block of labour.

actions.label: Complete the repair order (+3 coins, 1 labour)
actions.explain: A nearby settlement pays for one urgent repair after the workshop has power.

actions.label: Repair the signal mast (1 labour)
actions.explain: Use a crew shift to reconnect the mast once the workshop has power. This opens a remote repair contract.

actions.label: Buy mast parts and reconnect it (3 coins)
actions.explain: Purchase the missing transmitter parts and connect the mast without using today's crew shift.

actions.label: Deliver the remote repair contract (+4 coins, 1 labour)
actions.explain: With the workshop powered and the signal mast connected, take one distant community's repair order.

actions.label: Reserve the orchard harvest for the commons (1 labour)
actions.explain: Store the first harvest for neighbours. This reduces gathering supplies from four coins to two.

actions.label: Sell the orchard harvest at market (+3 coins, 1 labour)
actions.explain: Trade the first crop for three coins. The cash can outfit the boat or fund shared supplies.

actions.label: Open the commons with stored food (2 coins, 1 labour)
actions.explain: Use the reserved orchard harvest to host a gathering with fewer purchased supplies. Needs shelter, garden, orchard, two coins and a crew shift.

actions.label: Open the commons with a harvest gathering (4 coins, 1 labour)
actions.explain: Celebrate a safe local food and water network. Needs a repaired shelter, the garden, the orchard and four coins for shared supplies.

actions.label: Launch the canal trade route (2 coins, 1 labour)
actions.explain: Connect the repaired infrastructure to neighbours. Needs the crossing, pump and orchard, plus two coins to outfit the first boat.

actions.label: Meet supplier registration rules (3 personal coins + 1 workday)
actions.explain: Procurement requires supplier registration, insurance and tax documentation. You pay these costs from your own money while camping, with no guarantee of being selected.

actions.label: Award the contract to the project originator (3 committee coins)
actions.explain: You completed supplier requirements at personal cost. If selected, the committee pays for wiring, records your contribution, and keeps the maintenance terms. Registration costs are not repaid.

actions.label: Government absorbs the project as an existing program
actions.explain: The department announces this was already part of its program, takes the grant and project control, and leaves the originator out of its account. Work may continue under the department while authorship and decision power move away from you.

actions.label: Delegate the work to a political backer (3 public coins)
actions.explain: A politically connected contractor gets the wiring contract. It receives public money and the committee chair expects future political support. The project may serve residents while your work stays uncredited and maintenance is unfunded.

actions.label: Challenge the takeover (2 personal coins + 1 workday)
actions.explain: Spend scarce funds and time contesting the department claim and omission of your authorship. The complaint is reviewed after rest; refusal leaves the department in control and the money spent.

actions.label: Teach the crew your integration know-how (1 workday, unpaid)
actions.explain: Choose to share what you know without a contract. It costs a workday and earns no money or guaranteed credit. The crew gains practical capability, while you remain the knowledge holder; others may still control and claim the project.
